 Sri Lanka ‘A’ Captain Pavan Rathnayake gives the thumbs up sign before the team’s departure
 Two of the most exciting young players Sineth Jayawardena and Sharujan Shanmuganathan
 Pavan Rathnayake makes debut as national team Captain 
 Two-time winners of the Asia Cup Rising Stars (formerly known as ACC Emerging Teams Asia Cup), Sri Lanka ‘A’ led by outstanding white ball cricketer Pavan Rathnayake left for Doha Qatar on Monday to participate in the eighth edition of the tournament.
Sri Lanka ‘A’ grouped with Bangladesh ‘A’, Afghanistan ‘A’ and Hong Kong China in Group A are looking forward to topping the group and qualifying for the semi-finals in this eight-nation tournament that will run from 19-29 November featuring 15 ODIs across venues like the West End Park International Cricket Stadium and the University of Doha for Science and Technology.
“Against any opposition if we play well on that day there is every possible chance of finishing on the winning side,” said Sri Lanka ‘A’ Head Coach Ashan Priyanjan before the team’s departure.
“Throughout one whole month we had a good training session. Virtually all the players in the squad were involved playing in the Mercantile matches and they got some exposure playing white ball cricket.
“Last year some of the players played in Qatar and the information we have from them is that the wickets are a bit on the slow side. Oman pitches were also expected to be slow but if you look at some of the under 19 matches they turned out to be good surfaces. We have prepared ourselves to play on all kinds of surfaces. I am confident that we can give a good account of ourselves against all opposition,” he said.
Skipper Rathnayake in his first assignment as a national team captain said,” We have two games and we need to finish on top of our group. We are planning to take it step by step. We have a good balanced side and hope to give off our best.”
On his captaincy, Rathnayake said, “I have captained at school so captaincy is no issue. I am prepared to play my normal game.”
A lot will depend on Rathnayake who was the leading run scorer in the recently concluded Pakistan ODI Tri-Nation series where he accumulated 427 runs at an average of 106.75 in 5 innings and scored 2 centuries and 2 fifties against Pakistan and England.  
Apart from Rathnayake there is also the experience of Janith Liyanage, Nishan Madushka, Lasith Croospulle and Lahiru Samarakoon.
Sri Lanka ‘A’ play Afghanistan ‘A’ in their opening match on 19 November followed by the match against Hong Kong China on 21 November and Bangladesh ‘A’ on 23 November. The top two teams from each group qualify for the semi-finals. Group B comprises Pakistan ‘A’, India ‘A’, Nepal and UAE.
Sri Lanka ‘A’ were two-times winners in 2017 and 2018 and were runners-up in 2024. Pakistan ‘A’ are the reigning champions having won the last edition in 2025. They also won it twice before in 2019 and 2023. Surprisingly, India ‘A’ have won it only once – the inaugural tournament in 2013, and Afghanistan ‘A’ once in 2024.     
Sri Lanka ‘A’: Lasith Croospulle, Sineth Jayawardena, Nishan Madushka, Pavan Rathnayake (Captain), Nipun Dhananjaya, Chamika Heenatigala, Janith Liyanage, Sharujan Shanmuganathan, Ravindu Fernando, Vijayakanth Viyaskanth, Wanuja Sahan, Dulaj Samuditha, Duvindu Ranatunga, Lahiru Samarakoon, Garuka Sanketh. (ST)
